definitions.gloss: May blues; a state of lethargy or depression affecting new employees and students in May
definitions.explanation: a form of adjustment disorder common in Japan, occurring around May when the initial excitement of a new job or school year wears off and reality sets in after the Golden Week holiday

examples.japanese: {新入社員|しんにゅうしゃいん}は{五月病|ごがつびょう}になりやすい。
examples.english: New employees are prone to May blues.

examples.japanese: ゴールデンウィーク{明|あ}けに{五月病|ごがつびょう}になった。
examples.english: I got the May blues after Golden Week ended.

examples.japanese: {五月病|ごがつびょう}を{防|ふせ}ぐには、{無理|むり}をせず{休養|きゅうよう}を{取|と}ることが{大事|だいじ}だ。
examples.english: To prevent May blues, it's important to rest and not push yourself too hard.

notes:
FORMS:
{五月|ごがつ} (May) + {病|びょう} (illness) → May sickness

CULTURAL NOTE:
In Japan, the fiscal and academic year begins in April. By May, after the long Golden Week holiday (ゴールデンウィーク), new employees and students often experience:
- Loss of motivation
- Fatigue and exhaustion
- Difficulty adjusting to new environment
- Feelings of inadequacy

SYMPTOMS:
- やる{気|き}が{出|で}ない (lack of motivation)
- {疲|つか}れやすい (easily tired)
- {食欲|しょくよく}がない (loss of appetite)
- {眠|ねむ}れない (insomnia)

RELATED WORDS:
- {適応障害|てきおうしょうがい} (adjustment disorder)
- {燃|も}え{尽|つ}き{症候群|しょうこうぐん} (burnout syndrome)
- {新生活|しんせいかつ} (new life/lifestyle)
